title: TIC monthly release (February 2027 data) — an April REVISION edition, the clean-axis test the Feb/Mar exclusion never had, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,179 bytes) by the tic-monthly-2027-03-18 initial research — its 2027 table's April row reads '15' in the Monthly column with BOTH quarterly columns EMPTY and '30 - final' standing in the separate 'Annual: Foreign portfolio holdings of U.S. securities at end-June of previous year' column, under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. A single-cut monthly release, with the FINAL annual survey as a distinct release fifteen days later — read that way deliberately, since misreading a separate dated column as a component of the row is the error this table has now produced three times (see notes). Reference month February 2027 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. Corroborated mechanically and EXACTLY, which is stronger than the March sibling managed: April 2027 carries no 5 U.S.C. 6103 federal holiday, and the 11th business day of April 2027 is 2027-04-15 — an offset of +0 inside the page's '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule, an exact hit rather than the +3 outer edge 2027-03-18 sits at. Like March, April discriminates nothing between the holiday-aware and holiday-blind conventions, and that is stated rather than smoothed. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep: the proposer may not confirm what it found, only the event's own session may. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-monthly-2027-03-18 initial research (2026-09-09), the next unclaimed monthly slot after 2027-03-18. IT HAS A SPECIFIC AND OVERDUE JOB: it is the CLEAN-AXIS test for FT-tic-monthly-2027-01-19-3's revision-edition effect, which two sessions running have now weakened without being able to measure. April is a Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct REVISION edition under Treasury's note (c) ('The January, April, July, and October releases reflect revised data for the past year'), and unlike every prior candidate it is NOT entangled with the disputed Feb/Mar bucket: tic-monthly-2027-02-18 found it could not be the ordinary control it was filed as because it is a February vintage drawn from the excluded class, and tic-monthly-2027-03-18 found March cannot isolate anything either. April is neither. It is also the edition standing eleven business days (fifteen calendar days) before the FINAL annual survey (2027-04-30, April's last business day, already proposed as tic-annual-survey-final-2027-04-30), which is the pairing note (d) describes for the post-2011 regime — so the survey's benchmark reaching the monthly series through a revision edition is observable here rather than argued. AND ITS CORRIDOR IS CLEAN, WHICH NO RECENT SIBLING'S IS. tic-monthly-2027-03-18 measured that its own scored session sits at FOMC+2 and a quad-witching, with the March FOMC landing inside the TIC publication window in 12 of 14 years 2014-2027 — a structural collision that makes any March tape read uninterpretable. April 2027's FOMC is 2027-04-28, thirteen days later; the April monthly opex is 2027-04-16, the scored session, which that same session measured as irrelevant to the 10-year (monthly opex 3.398bp, n=93, vs 4.017bp non-expiration, p=0.64). So April is the first monthly slot in this series since 2027-01-19 that can carry a tape test attributable to the print. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
